Subject: Marketplace invoicing & tax: Seller-of-Record vs Platform billing — initial questions

Hi all,

Following our co-sell kickoff with Acme, a couple of billing/tax clarifications came up that will affect how we structure the contract and the invoice flow for the pilot. High level: Acme prefers a single invoice they can pay (their AP team asked for one line item for the Redwood subscription), but AWS/Azure billing models differ on whether Redwood or the cloud marketplace is the biller of record. Key asks below.

Questions: 
- For AWS Marketplace (SaaS subscriptions) — if we list via AWS with AWS as the billing intermediary, does AWS issue the invoice to Acme and remit net to Redwood (i.e., AWS collects VAT where required)? If so, what documentation do they need from us (W-9 / W-8 / tax residency docs)?
- For Azure Marketplace — if Microsoft is the biller/reseller, will invoices show Microsoft as the vendor and include VAT for EU buyers? What supporting docs does Microsoft require for non-US sellers to avoid backup withholding?
- For GCP Marketplace (if applicable) — is there a difference when using Marketplace or using a direct-billing SKU?

Immediate constraints from Acme: they want a single payable invoice in EUR with VAT treatment clear on the line item. Their finance contact is CC'd. They will not accept two separate invoices (one from marketplace + one from Redwood) unless there is a clear reconciliation line.

Attachments: AWS billing schema v2 (draft) and my signed W-9 (for AWS review).

Action requested: AWS/Azure reps — can you confirm the typical invoicing flow and the minimal tax docs required? Grace/Lauren — once we have vendor answers, can you map to three recommended flows (AWS-billed, Azure-billed, Redwood-billed) including pros/cons for Acme and the implications for revenue recognition / tax reporting?

Thanks,

Thanks Ben — quick internal note before we hear from partners:

Short summary from ops experience:
- AWS: two primary models — "AWS billed" (AWS invoices customer, collects payment, remits to seller) vs "Seller billed" (seller invoices customer directly). When AWS invoices, the invoice will typically show AWS as the biller; VAT handling is driven by buyer location and seller registration. AWS will request W-9 for US entities or W-8BEN-E for non-US entities for tax withholding determinations.
- Azure: Microsoft Marketplace often acts as the aggregator (Microsoft invoices the customer). Microsoft may apply VAT based on the buyer VAT registration; for EU B2B sales with valid VAT ID, reverse charge can apply. Microsoft requires vendor tax profile info (country, VAT number, tax classification).
- GCP: similar split — if you use Google Cloud Marketplace metering, Google may invoice; direct SKUs can be billed directly by vendor.

Risks for Acme: If the marketplace is the biller, Acme will receive an invoice from the marketplace (AWS/MS/Google) with marketplace fees and the seller settlement happens separately. Acme's AP team wants one invoice showing Redwood as the provider — that will likely require us to be the biller or to provide a consolidated invoice for their reconciliation.

I'll draft the three flow diagrams and a compliance checklist (tax forms, VAT evidence, vendor numbers) once partners confirm the exact doc names they require.

Hi Ben / Grace / Lauren / Acme,

Thanks for the clear note. A few clarifications from Microsoft side:

1) Invoice flow (Microsoft as biller): Microsoft issues the invoice to the customer (Acme). The invoice will contain the product line and the gross amount billed to the customer. Microsoft's settlement statement to the publisher (Redwood) shows the net after Microsoft marketplace fees.

2) VAT handling: For B2B customers in the EU with a valid VAT number, the invoice will typically be zero-rated for VAT (reverse charge) if the VAT ID is validated at purchase. If the buyer does not provide a VAT ID, Microsoft will charge VAT at the local rate and remit it.

3) Required vendor documentation: We require publisher tax profile details (legal entity name, country of registration, VAT number if applicable), and for US entities a completed W-9 (for our records). For non-US entities, we accept W-8BEN-E. Please upload documentation to the Partner Center tax profile.

4) Single-invoice requirement: If Acme needs Redwood listed as the vendor on the invoice for internal procurement controls, you have two practical options: (a) Redwood invoices Acme directly (Redwood-billed flow) and we do a marketplace-only listing without using Microsoft as the biller, or (b) Microsoft invoices, and Redwood provides a secondary consolidated invoice to Acme that notes the Microsoft invoice number for reconciliation (this can be a custom bookkeeping document, but Microsoft will still be the legal seller on the marketplace invoice). Note that option (b) can complicate AP/AR for both parties and can affect how VAT is reported.

I'll add a short guidance doc to Partner Center and include links to the Partner Center tax profile form.

Best,

Thanks Katerina and team — helpful context. Quick summary and our recommended next steps for Acme pilot (to be shared with their AP):

Decision framework (short):
- If Acme requires "Redwood as vendor on the invoice": pursue Redwood-billed flow. Pros: single invoice (meets Acme AP), full control of VAT treatment on our invoice. Cons: limits ability to use marketplace promotional credits and some co-sell programs that require marketplace billing. Implications: Redwood must be set up for cross-border VAT reporting and we may need to register for VAT in buyer jurisdictions.

- If marketplace billing is preferable to reduce operational overhead for Redwood: use AWS/Azure/GCP billed flows but provide a reconciliation invoice to Acme that references the marketplace invoice number. Pros: simpler seller settlement (platform handles payments/VAT in many cases). Cons: Acme might push back on paying two documents and we must ensure reconciliation matches net amounts.

Action items (owners & timeline):
1) Grace: Draft three short flow diagrams + compliance checklist (tax forms required, where to upload) — due EOD Aug 6.
2) Lauren: Confirm with Revenue team how marketplace-settled revenue should be recognized vs Redwood-billed revenue; flag any SOC/accounting impacts — due Aug 10.
3) Ben: Coordinate with Acme AP on whether they will accept a secondary Redwood consolidated invoice or insist Redwood is the legal vendor — Ben to confirm by Aug 5.
4) Partners (AWS/Azure): please confirm minimal tax docs and link to intake forms; AWS please confirm whether your marketplace requires W-9 for US sellers and whether AWS will collect VAT on behalf of sellers in the EU.

Acme AP — can you confirm by EOD Aug 6 which flow you will accept? If you want Redwood on the single vendor line, we will start with Redwood-billed pilot and document VAT registration needs.

I'll collate answers into a short playbook for future marketplace listings and co-sell deals.
